knowHow.text: Filament S-Flex Carbon is an innovative 3D printing material that seamlessly combines the flexibility of traditional flex filament with the added strength and durability provided by a 20% carbon fiber reinforcement.
The carbon reinforces the TPU and makes it more resistant and stiffer.
The material is also very easy to process and has very low warping.
In addition, an excellent carbon look is created.
Note: Due to the abrasive nature of the carbon fibers, a hardened nozzle (e.g., hardened steel or ruby nozzle) is strongly recommended.
Additionally, a nozzle diameter of at least 0.6 mm should be used to prevent clogging and ensure smooth extrusion.
The increased stiffness makes the filament easier to print than other flexible TPU materials.

FiberFlex CF is ideal for applications requiring a combination of flexibility and strength—such as shock absorbers, gaskets, protective components, industrial structures, or mechanical parts exposed to heavy loads and harsh conditions.

polymerEnvironment.finding: Ketones such as acetone, methylethylketone (MEK) and cyclohexanone are partial solvents for thermoplastic polyurethane elastomers. Elastollan products are unsuitable for long-term use in these solvents. Methyl ethyl ketone: volume swelling 105 % / 110 % / 130 %, reduction of tensile strength 80 % / 80 % / 90 % (ester / C 85 A / ether); other short-chained aliphatic ketones such as acetone have a similar effect.

polymerEnvironment.finding: Aliphatic alcohols, such as ethanol and isopropanol, cause swelling of Elastollan products. This is combined with a loss of tensile strength. Ethanol: volume swelling 16 % / 18 % / 33 %, reduction of tensile strength 52 % / 52 % / 64 % (ester / C 85 A / ether); after evaporation of the solvents the tensile strength recovers approximately its original value.

polymerEnvironment.finding: Contact of Elastollan with aromatic hydrocarbons such as benzene and toluene results in considerable swelling even at room temperature. polymerEnvironment.agent: Lubricating oils and greases (IRM 901, 902, 903 test oils)
polymerEnvironment.conditions: Immersion at room temperature; 3 weeks at 100 °C
polymerEnvironment.finding: No reduction in strength occurs after immersion in test oils IRM 901, IRM 902, and IRM 903 at room temperature. There is also no reduction in tensile strength after 3 weeks immersion at 100 °C. Elastollan is in principal resistant to lubricating oils and greases, however irreversible damage can be caused by included additives. Compatibility testing in each individual lubricant is to be recommended.
polymerEnvironment.locator: PDF p. 2 Lubricating oils and greases

polymerEnvironment.agent: Saturated hydrocarbons (diesel oil, isooctane, petroleum ether, kerosene)
polymerEnvironment.finding: Contact of Elastollan with saturated hydrocarbons such as diesel oil, isooctane, petroleum ether and kerosene results in a limited swelling. At room temperature, this swelling amounts to approx. 1-3 % and the resultant reduction in tensile strength is no more than 20 %. After evaporation and reversal of the swelling, the original mechanical properties are almost completely restored.

polymerEnvironment.agent: Hot water, moisture vapour, tropical climate (polyester-based TPU)
polymerEnvironment.finding: If polyester based polyurethanes are exposed for lengthy periods to hot water, moisture vapor or tropical climates, an irreversible break-down of the polyester chains occurs through hydrolysis. This results in a reduction in mechanical properties. This effect is more marked in flexible grades. Due to a good stabilization, a degradation of polyester-based Elastollan is rarely experienced at room temperature.

polymerEnvironment.finding: Because of its chemical structure, polyether-based Elastollan is much more resistant to hydrolytic degradation (Figures 41 and 42 compare Elastollan 1185 A ether grade with C 85 A ester grade between 50 and 100 °C).

polymerEnvironment.finding: Plastics are chemically degraded by the effect of UV radiation. The degree of ageing depends on duration and intensity. In the case of polyurethanes, the effect is seen initially as surface embrittlement. This is accompanied by a yellowing in color and a reduction in mechanical properties. It is possible to improve UV resistance by addition of color pigments which prevent the deep penetration of UV rays... The ageing process can also be delayed by the addition of UV stabilizers.
